original_test_intent: Verify that the authenticated user's BMC Web profile displays the correct effective privilege and timezone display preference, and that both values remain readable and unchanged after a full browser F5 reload in the same authorized session.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC/WebUI build, approved test account and authoritative privilege/timezone values; establish the same-target browser session without exposing secrets; open the user Profile settings and capture account marker, User Privilege and Timezone display preference from non-edit mode; independently read supported backend account/timezone properties as corroboration; press F5 once from a safe non-submitting page; verify target/account/session continuity and recapture both values; compare exact/normalized timezone representation and role mapping; exit or leave session in approved state without changes.
manual_activity: An operator supplies/approves the account, authoritative privilege and timezone values and confirms visible UI correctness; browser automation may capture before/after F5 evidence without editing.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT firmware, WebUI and supported browser versions
Approved test username/account marker and authoritative effective role/privilege mapping; root is not assumed
Expected timezone display preference, canonical zone/offset/DST/locale formatting and backend source
Session timeout/refresh behavior, safe Profile page state, protected access and final session cleanup
safety_requirements: Verify the intended BMC and test account before capturing profile values
Use view-only page state and inspect DOM/screenshot without revealing credentials, cookies or tokens
Ensure F5 cannot resubmit an edit/password/profile form
Do not change privilege, timezone, password or session policy to make values match
Stop on wrong account/target, logout/CSRF error, ambiguous values, unexpected submit or value change
agent_execution_scope: Capture non-secret account marker, privilege and timezone before and after one F5
Corroborate values with approved read-only backend properties where supported
Compare normalized timezone and role while preserving literal UI rendering
Do not choose expected values, expose session artifacts, edit profile, repeatedly relogin or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve test account and effective privilege/role representation
Approve canonical timezone preference and UI/backend formatting/normalization including DST
Approve expected session persistence after F5 and final cleanup
Review UI/backend or before/after mismatch and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Browser capture is the correct source-facing method, but 'correct' needs authoritative privilege/timezone values and F5 must occur on a safe non-submitting view in the same session.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the approved browser session to capture literal/DOM privilege and timezone values, press F5 once on the read-only Profile view, recapture target/account/session and both values, and compare with approved backend references.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC Web Profile Information, User Privilege, Timezone display preference, F5 persistence and 5/5-minute estimate remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the GUI fields to one authenticated account and backend role/timezone sources, then assert target/session continuity plus literal and normalized value stability across a single full-page reload.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds account/target identity, authoritative references, timezone normalization, safe-page/F5 semantics, DOM evidence and secret protection.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A readable string is not proof of correctness; the profile could show a cached/default timezone or privilege for another account, and a refresh that logs in again would not demonstrate session-preserved state.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: WebUI may localize timezone labels or show role aliases rather than backend values, so equivalence rules must be approved rather than requiring naive text equality.

project_override_considerations: If root is specifically required, engineering must approve use of that account and its expected privilege; otherwise use a dedicated account to reduce exposure. A read-only API property can corroborate but cannot replace the source-required Profile/F5 display coverage.
expected_evidence: Authoritative privilege and timezone/locale/DST reference values
Secret-safe before-F5 full/DOM Profile evidence for account marker, User Privilege and Timezone preference
Secret-safe after-F5 target/account/session and both field values
Normalization/equality result plus approved backend corroboration
No-submit/no-change audit, session cleanup/errors and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require privilege and timezone profile data to remain correct/readable after F5. The root example and expected values require project definition but do not contradict the test.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The read-only GUI workflow is clear. Approved account, expected values and browser access are normal prerequisites, so the case remains conditionally executable.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2244 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00026-V001: approve the BMC/WebUI/browser and test account (including whether root is mandatory), authoritative effective User Privilege/role and backend mapping, expected Timezone display preference with canonical zone/offset/DST/locale normalization, same-session behavior after F5, safe page/CSRF handling, protected evidence and final session cleanup.

review_improvement: Preserves the two Profile fields and F5 behavior while preventing the wrong account, cached/default values or a hidden relogin from satisfying the source's correctness criterion.
independent_technical_reasoning: Privilege and timezone are user-profile properties with different authoritative sources: role comes from account policy, while displayed timezone may be a per-user preference transformed by locale and DST. Their strings can remain unchanged across F5 yet still be wrong, or legitimately render differently while representing the same zone. The test therefore needs approved references, account identity and normalization in addition to before/after UI evidence. Because the source specifically requires BMC Web and an authenticated profile, user/browser confirmation remains part of execution despite the observation being read-only.
